# Anova



```{r}
# === 1. Read the pilot data ===

# Replace with the actual path to your CSV file
pilot_data <- d %>% 
  filter(!FeatureMatch %in% c("SelfPair"))

# Check column names
str(pilot_data)

# === 2. Summarize the data: means and SDs per FeatureMatch ===

# Compute group means
group_means <- tapply(pilot_data$Response, pilot_data$FeatureMatch, mean)

# Compute pooled within-group SD
group_sds <- tapply(pilot_data$Response, pilot_data$FeatureMatch, sd)

# Compute pooled SD (assumes equal group sizes or similar SDs)
pooled_sd <- sqrt(mean(group_sds^2))  # a simple approximation

# === 3. Compute effect size ===

k <- length(group_means)  # number of levels
grand_mean <- mean(group_means)

# Between-group SS
ss_between <- sum((group_means - grand_mean)^2)

# MS between
ms_between <- ss_between / (k - 1)

# MS within (approximate from pooled SD)
ms_within <- pooled_sd^2

# Eta squared
eta_squared <- ss_between / (ss_between + ms_within * (k - 1))

# Cohen's f
cohen_f <- sqrt(eta_squared / (1 - eta_squared))

# Output effect size
cat("Group means:\n")
print(round(group_means, 2))
cat("\nPooled within-group SD:", round(pooled_sd, 2), "\n")
cat("Eta squared (η²):", round(eta_squared, 3), "\n")
cat("Cohen's f:", round(cohen_f, 3), "\n\n")

# === 4. Power analysis ===

# Calculate required total sample size for 80% power
power_result <- pwr.anova.test(
  k = k,
  f = cohen_f,
  sig.level = 0.05,
  power = 0.80
)

cat("Required total sample size for 80% power:", ceiling(power_result$n), "\n")
cat("≈", ceiling(power_result$n / k), "participants per FeatureMatch (if between-subjects)\n")

```

```{r}
# === 3. Generate power curve ===

# Define sample sizes to test (per group)
n_per_group <- seq(5, 100, by = 1)
total_n <- n_per_group * k

# Compute power for each sample size
power_vals <- sapply(n_per_group, function(n) {
  pwr.anova.test(k = k, f = cohen_f, n = n, sig.level = 0.05)$power
})

# Create dataframe for plotting
power_df <- data.frame(
  Total_N = total_n,
  Power = power_vals
)

# Plot power curve (updated for ggplot2 >= 3.4.0)
ggplot(power_df, aes(x = Total_N, y = Power)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.80, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Power Curve for One-Way ANOVA",
    x = "Total Sample Size",
    y = "Statistical Power"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```


```{r}
# Repeated-measures ANOVA
anova_rm <- aov_car(Response ~ FeatureMatch + Error(ID.Ibex/FeatureMatch), data = pilot_data)
summary(anova_rm)


# Estimated marginal means and pairwise comparisons
emmeans_result <- emmeans(anova_rm, ~ FeatureMatch)
pairs(emmeans_result)


eta_squared(anova_rm, partial = TRUE)

# Convert η² = 0.29 to Cohen's f, then d for paired t
f <- sqrt(0.29 / (1 - 0.29))     # ≈ 0.64
d <- f * sqrt(2)                 # for two FeatureMatchs (d ≈ 0.91)

# Power for paired t-test
pwr.t.test(d = d, power = 0.80, sig.level = 0.05, type = "paired", alternative = "two.sided")

pwr.t.test(d = 0.61, power = 0.80, sig.level = 0.05, type = "paired", alternative = "two.sided")


```

```{r}
d_vals <- seq(10, 40, by = 1)
power_vals <- sapply(d_vals, function(n) {
  pwr.t.test(d = 0.61, n = n, sig.level = 0.05, type = "paired")$power
})

plot(d_vals, power_vals, type = "b", pch = 19,
     xlab = "Sample Size (ID.Ibexs)", ylab = "Power",
     main = "Power Curve for Paired t-test (d = 0.61)")
abline(h = 0.8, col = "red", lty = 2)
```

```{r}
pilot_data$FeatureMatch <- factor(pilot_data$FeatureMatch)

simulate_power_lmer <- function(
  pilot_model,
  pilot_data,
  subject_col = "Subject",
  n_subjects = NULL,
  n_trials_per_condition = 5,
  n_simulations = 500,
  alpha = 0.05
) {

  
  pilot_data <- pilot_data %>%
    mutate(Subject = factor(.data[[subject_col]]))
  
  cond_levels <- levels(pilot_data$FeatureMatch)
  pilot_data$FeatureMatch <- factor(pilot_data$FeatureMatch, levels = cond_levels)
  
  n_conditions <- length(cond_levels)
  
  pilot_subjects <- unique(pilot_data$Subject)
  n_pilot_subjects <- length(pilot_subjects)
  
  if (is.null(n_subjects)) {
    n_subjects <- n_pilot_subjects
  }
  
  fixef_vals <- fixef(pilot_model)
  print("Fixed effects:")
  print(fixef_vals)
  print("FeatureMatch levels:")
  print(cond_levels)
  
  vc <- as.data.frame(VarCorr(pilot_model))
  subj_sd <- vc[vc$grp == "Subject", "sdcor"]
  if (length(subj_sd) == 0 || is.na(subj_sd)) subj_sd <- 5
  resid_sd <- sigma(pilot_model)
  
  base_data <- expand.grid(
    Subject = factor(1:n_subjects),
    FeatureMatch = factor(cond_levels, levels = cond_levels),
    Trial = 1:n_trials_per_condition
  )
  
  get_fixed_effect <- function(fe, cond) {
    intercept <- fe[1]
    
    cond_effect <- sapply(as.character(cond), function(cn) {
      name <- paste0("FeatureMatch", cn)
      if (name %in% names(fe)) {
        val <- fe[name]
        as.numeric(val)
      } else {
        0
      }
    })
    
    intercept + cond_effect
  }
  
  results <- replicate(n_simulations, {
    subj_intercepts <- rnorm(n_subjects, mean = 0, sd = subj_sd)
    
    sim_data <- base_data %>%
      mutate(
        subj_int = subj_intercepts[as.numeric(Subject)],
        fixed = get_fixed_effect(fixef_vals, FeatureMatch),
        Response = fixed + subj_int + rnorm(n(), 0, resid_sd)
      )
    
    mod_sim <- lmer(Response ~ FeatureMatch + (1 | Subject), data = sim_data)
    
    emm <- emmeans(mod_sim, ~ FeatureMatch)
    contrast_res <- contrast(emm, method = list(
      val_vs_concept = c(0, 0, 1, -1)
    ))
    
    pval <- summary(contrast_res)$p.value
    
    as.numeric(pval < alpha)
  })
  
  power_estimate <- mean(results)
  cat("Estimated power with", n_subjects, "subjects:", round(power_estimate, 3), "\n")
  return(power_estimate)
}



power <- simulate_power_lmer(
  pilot_model,
  pilot_data,
  subject_col = "ID.Ibex",
  n_subjects = 30,
  n_simulations = 500
)


```

# Power curve
```{r}
subject_counts <- seq(10, 100, by = 10)  # e.g., from 10 to 100 subjects, by 10

power_results <- sapply(subject_counts, function(n) {
  simulate_power_lmer(
    pilot_model,
    pilot_data,
    subject_col = "ID.Ibex",
    n_subjects = n,
    n_simulations = 200  # fewer sims for speed; increase if you want more precision
  )
})

power_df <- data.frame(
  Subjects = subject_counts,
  Power = power_results
)


ggplot(power_df, aes(x = Subjects, y = Power)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.80, linetype = "dashed", color = "red") +
  labs(
    title = "Power Curve for Mixed Model",
    x = "Number of Subjects",
    y = "Estimated Power"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)

```
